Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

We will continue with module seven on functional materials that is polymers and this will be the last class of this module.

Key details

  • In this class we are going to talk about molecular weight of polymers.
  • That is number average molecular weight, weight average molecular weight, and viscosity average molecular weight.
  • We know that its molecular weight is eighteen, and irrespective of the source from where we are going to take the water, the molecular weight is going to still be eighteen, and each of the molecule is going to have a molecular weight of 18, but the case of polymers is different because in a sample the molecular weight of the polymers, the chain length of the polymers is different.
  • Each unit may have a different.
  • Therefore, whenever we talk about molecular weight of a polymer, we talk about an average molecular weight.
  • So this molecular weight now we know is a very important characteristic of a polymer sample because several properties of polymers are found to depend on the molecular weight.
  • The entire range of mechanical properties which are very useful to determine the application of a polymer like stress strain, impact, fracture, fatigue, creep, stress relaxation, and cracking, they are all influenced by the average molecular weight and also the molecular weight distribution.
  • There could be number average molecular weight, we can also have a weight average molecular weight and also viscosity average molecular weight.
